correctness.rationale: The polynomial g=1+x^2+x^4+x^5+x^6+x^10+x^11 has degree 11 and divides x^23+1, so all 2^12 messages with degree<12 map injectively to 4096 distinct codewords. For each nonconstant codeword its cyclic zero-run lengths r give w_b=23-sum max(r-b+1,0); the 81-class run census therefore determines all 23 complete b-symbol distributions. Inspected actual GENERATE.py, VERIFY.py, both CSVs. A separate independently written enumerator generated 4096 words, computed every one of 23 cyclic-window spectra and all 81 zero-run multiplicities, confirming all values and the 23 common cyclic-generator-orbit minimizers for b=3..11. The ordinary b=1 code weight enumerator, known minimum b distances and saturated 12..23 widths were checked separately. This is a finite exhaustive computation for the exact code, with an injectivity proof; it asserts no general arbitrary-code result.

evidence: Guan, Luo, Luo, Fei and Wang, Generalized Repetition Codes and Their Application to HARQ (https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15207): Example 4 displays (7,11,13,15,16,17,18,19,20,21,22). Reciprocal code reverses coordinate order and preserves cyclic b-window spectra.

Vega, The b-symbol weight distributions of all semiprimitive irreducible cyclic codes (https://doi.org/10.1007/s10623-023-01193-w): Golay has seven nonzero ordinary Hamming weights and reducible parity-check polynomial; family constraints exclude it.

Shi, Özbudak and Solé, Geometric Approach to b-Symbol Hamming Weights of Cyclic Codes (https://doi.org/10.1109/TIT.2021.3069772): General stabilizing count gives 4095 nonzero words with weight23 at b>=12 but not finite widths 2..11 coefficients.
Resultary published SCOPE080, three binary cyclic symbol-pair codes (https://github.com/Resultary/2026/tree/main/2026/9/8/SCOPE080): Separate finite codes do not dominate [23,12,7] b-symbol spectra.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Vega's general b-spectrum theorems impose irreducible/semiprimitive code hypotheses excluded by Golay's reducible parity-check; Shi–Özbudak–Solé general stabilization covers only high-width trivial rows. Neither dominates the 81-partition refinement and widths 2..11.

originality.rationale: The b-symbol minimum-distance values for widths 1–11 were published explicitly by Guan et al, Example 4, using the reciprocal Golay generator. Wide-width stabilization is general prior theory and the run-to-window identity is elementary/known. The surviving novel claim is the nontrivial full weight-multiplicity spectra and 81-class run-partition refinement, plus equality of all width-3..11 minimizing word sets with one 23-word orbit. No inspected prior table yields those stronger multiplicity statements, but code-table priority risk remains.
residual_risks: Complete binary Golay b-symbol weight enumerators or a reciprocal-version run census may exist in unindexed coding-theory tables or theses.
Known b=1 Golay Hamming enumerator, b=1..11 minimum *values*, and b>=12 stabilization must not be rebranded as original.

value.rationale: This is a complete and independently reproducible symbol-read spectrum for the canonical perfect binary Golay code, useful for enumerator-based error-detection/coding analyses. Full multiplicity profiles distinguish codes/read lengths with identical minimum distance, and the common-minimizer orbit identifies exact extremizers. A complete finite classification of a central natural object has scientific value despite no general b-symbol theorem.

limitations: Complete binary Golay b-symbol weight enumerators or a reciprocal-version run census may exist in unindexed coding-theory tables or theses.
Known b=1 Golay Hamming enumerator, b=1..11 minimum *values*, and b>=12 stabilization must not be rebranded as original.
The assessment gives a qualified priority judgment; finite computations prove only the exact finite ranges exhausted and do not substitute for general arguments.
